To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) cognitive load was not a factor in the performance of the participants on the tasks, (b) the participants' performance was not affected by the type of interface, (c) the participants' preferences for the type of interface was not related to their performance, and (d) the participants' preference for a type of interface was related to their performance.

the use of a knowledge-based interface in an interactive information retrieval system does not improve the performance of a user who is already familiar with a conventional interface, but that the knowledge-based interface is superior to the conventional one for a novice user.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and evaluation of bibliographic information retrieval systems that are more compatible with human cognitive processes than existing systems.
the design of a cognitive system which can be described as a system of knowledge and reasoning.
the design of a system that can help users in their information seeking process, and that can also be easily used by the users.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of the computer in information retrieval is a complex process which requires a thorough analysis of the problem and of the available techniques and tools, and which can only be solved in the context of a well-defined information system.
the cognitive model is a very useful tool for designing user-friendly information retrieval systems.
the cognitive compatibility of bibliographic retrieval systems is a complex function of many factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have been developing a system which is capable of understanding and answering questions in the context of a particular information domain, and which can be used as an interface to information retrieval systems.
we need a cognitive model of the user, a model of the information, and a model of the system.

the cognitive compatibility of information retrieval systems can be increased by using a combination of the following techniques: (1) the use of knowledge-based methods for the representation and retrieval of knowledge, (2) the use of artificial intelligence techniques for identifying and representing the user's knowledge, and (3) the use of human factors techniques for identifying and designing the user interface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is an opportunity for cognitive compatibility to be used as a design heuristic to help guide the design and development of IR interfaces.

we should not be surprised that the human brain has evolved to be good at the kinds of problems that it has been faced with in the environment, and not be good at problems that it has never encountered in the environment.
the use of the cognitive model of information retrieval (CMIR) can be a useful tool for improving the design of bibliographic information retrieval (BIR) systems.
